quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Riding gloves are usually made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe motorcycle riding gear includes a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
Easier to see than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flashing your brake light before you slow down or stop helps other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need regular checking?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small mechanical problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If possible, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: The correct body position on a motorcycle is:

options.text: Sitting forward enough so your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
Sitting as far back as possible and stretching to reach the grips.
Leaning over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keeping your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sitting forward enough so your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips. This lets you easily reach and operate the controls.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided since other drivers see you easily.
Are only recommended in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning routine. This helps you stay aware of what is behind you.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like food and drinks. This means:

options.text: Within minutes of drinking, alcohol reaches the brain and affects you.
It takes a long time to feel the effects.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes of drinking, alcohol reaches the brain and affects you.
questions.explanation: Because it does not need to be digested, alcohol enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes. Your body gets rid of about one drink per hour.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of a lane?
questions.explanation: Car drippings create an oily strip in the center of lanes. Motorcycles can usually operate safely on this center strip when conditions are dry.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery for motorcycles?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are slippery surfaces. Ride with extra caution on these surfaces.

questions.question: When does alcohol impairment start?

options.text: At about half of the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired even if your blood alcohol is below the legal limit. Do not drink any alcohol before riding.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How can you make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Attach a large flag to the frame.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright, reflective clothing and use your turn signals and brake light.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Choose a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to increase your speed.
Only when there is a lot of traffic.
Every time you plan to change lanes.
Only when it is dark outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: What does a DOT-approved helmet do?

options.text: Greatly reduces the severity of a head injury.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Greatly reduces the severity of a head injury.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet does not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: One front brake and one rear brake.
Two front brakes, one rear brake, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: One front brake and one rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a bridge grating?

options.text: Ride on the far right side of the lane.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is normal and not dangerous. Keep a steady speed and ride straight. Zigzagging to correct the weave is dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike since all bikes are similar.
Check the controls and learn the shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works properly.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and learn the shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes several times first.

questions.question: In West Virginia, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: In West Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator?
questions.explanation: On a motorcycle, the accelerator is at the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is used for:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs tell drivers about road rules, like speed limits. These signs are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle you haven't used before, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride normally, since all bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Learn how the new motorcycle works before you ride it. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: What brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Squeeze the front brake until it locks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time. Do not squeeze the front brake too hard. Never lock the brakes.
